# PRB-006: The app hostname answers over HTTPS without TLS or redirect anomalies

- **Group:** Outside view
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

Given an app hostname, stackward probe requests https://<hostname>/ with normal certificate verification and follows redirects on the same hostname only (at most 10). A redirect loop usually means the app redirects to HTTPS on its own while a tunnel or proxy in front already terminates TLS and talks plain HTTP to it. A redirect from HTTPS down to HTTP, a certificate that fails verification or expires within 14 days, and a 5xx answer are reported as warnings. Redirects to another host are recorded but not followed. Without a hostname this check is skipped.

## Verify by hand

```sh
curl -sv -o /dev/null --max-redirs 10 -L https://app.example.com/ 2>&1 | grep -E '^< (HTTP|location)|expire'
```

## How to fix it

Behind a tunnel, turn off the app's own redirect to HTTPS (or trust the proxy's X-Forwarded-Proto) and let the tunnel enforce HTTPS; renew or fix the certificate when verification fails.

## What a fix can break

Turning off the app redirect while the app is also reachable directly serves it over plain HTTP; close direct access first (PRB-002).

Run `stackward explain PRB-006` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
